transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I've been having this issue with eating. When I'm alone at night, once I start, it just feels like something else takes over. I can't stop myself, even when I'm literally telling myself to put the food away. It's just out of my control.
Can you describe what it feels like when you're eating during these episodes? Do you feel like you're not in control of what or how much you're eating?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying. It's a complete lack of control. Once I start, it's like my brain just goes on autopilot. I'll be standing there, fully aware, literally telling myself in my head to just stop and put the food away, but I can't do it. My hands just keep going. I really have zero say in what or how much I'm eating until the whole thing is just... over.
Do these episodes cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah, they definitely cause me a lot of distress, and it is starting to interfere with things. Like, at work... recently I had to do this bilingual outreach presentation. I just got so distracted the whole time, mostly just thinking about leaving afterward so I could go home. I ended up stumbling through parts of it pretty badly. I'm really worried my coworkers noticed that something was off with me. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way of my normal life.
Do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal during these episodes?
I haven't really noticed that, honestly. I don't think I'm eating any faster than I usually do. It's more just... I can't stop once I start. But the actual pace feels pretty normal to me.
Do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full during these episodes?

Not really, no. I mean, I definitely eat a lot when it happens, but I don't usually push it to the point where I feel sick or painfully full. I just... I stop when the urge finally passes, or when I run out of whatever I'm eating. But physically, my stomach doesn't usually hurt from being too full or anything like that.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

No, not really. I mean, sometimes I happen to be alone just because I'm at home by myself after work, but I don't go out of my way to hide it. I'm not really embarrassed about the actual amount I'm eating if someone else is around. So, no, I wouldn't say I purposely isolate myself to do it.
Do you find yourself eating a much larger amount of food in one sitting than most people would eat in a similar period of time, say within a couple of hours?

Yeah, definitely. On nights after late shifts, I'll just... I can go through a lot. Like, I'll eat a whole frozen pizza, then move on to eating cereal straight out of the box, grab whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and just clear out whatever snacks are in the cabinet. All of that happens in maybe an hour or two. It's... yeah, it's way more than I'd ever eat in front of anyone else, for sure.
After these episodes, do you find yourself feeling guilty, depressed, or disgusted with yourself about how much you ate?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel great about it, obviously, but it's not this huge wave of guilt or anything. I don't really feel depressed or disgusted with myself afterwards. It's just... something that happens, I guess. I just kind of move on and go to bed.
How often do these episodes happen? Would you say they occur at least once a week on average?

Yeah, I'd say so. For at least the last four months, there's usually... well, at least one night a week where I'm alone and I just eat way more than I meant to. And then, I make myself throw up afterward.
Do you make yourself throw up after these eating episodes because you're worried about gaining weight or feeling like you've eaten too much?

Yeah, pretty much. After I eat like that, I usually just end up in the bathroom making myself throw up. It basically feels like the only way to undo it before the calories settle in. I just want to get rid of it so I don't gain the weight from all of that.
